synopsis: The UK regulatory review did not verify HSE, CPA, Strategic Forum or MPA guidance, leaving a verification gap despite Chapter 4's use of HSE statistics and guidance [f2226, f3204, f3205, f3206, f3207]. For 2025/26, HSE recorded 126 worker deaths across Great Britain; moving vehicles caused 24 deaths, the second-largest category after falls from height at 31, but these figures are not specific to mines, quarries or construction earthmovers [f3146, f3147]. Historical figures require reconciliation: the 2024/25 HSE release gives moving vehicles about 16% of fatal injuries and a preceding five-year average of around 21 deaths annually, whereas a vendor summary reports 14 of 124 deaths for 2024/25; the 2023/24 figures were 25 of 138 [f3149, f3150, f3152, f3151]. HSE's cross-industry guidance attributes nearly a quarter of workplace-transport deaths to reversing and notes costly damage from many reversing accidents without injuries [f3153, f3154]. Its undated quarry guidance attributes 40% of accidents and 60% of deaths to transport and states that seat belts would prevent 25% of all fatal quarry accidents; the lack of a date limits temporal interpretation [f3155, f3156, f3157].

relations.note: Both report 126 cross-industry worker deaths in Great Britain in 2025/26.
Both report 24 moving-vehicle deaths, second to 31 falls-from-height deaths.
Both attribute 40% of quarry accidents to transport in undated HSE guidance.
Both attribute 60% of quarry deaths to transport in undated HSE guidance.
Both describe costly property damage from non-injury reversing accidents.
For 2024/25, about 16% conflicts with the vendor's 14 of 124, approximately 11%.

Lower counts for other categories support moving vehicles' second-place ranking.
Adds transport's fatality share alongside its share of all quarry accidents.
Adds non-injury economic consequences to reversing's fatality burden.
